result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password or Bitwarden**\. Both offer proper business password management, secure sharing and centralised administration without needing a dedicated IT team.

My overall recommendation is **1Password for ease of use** and **Bitwarden for value for money**\.

## My top 5 recommendations

![1Password 8.12 - TidBITS](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/34HDvvYhqgd6AnMFmrlTm3hAXFxcbeGEwY_LB_XZ_XGVtrk4a2QxTEX-2LBZt2GGXhIIaKEolAWfkyjqt2bzeCs60tKyMvcGjArpm-vdyy1ZPxujq2f9_l2uItYJrXcwCcU9bPBSy8AGv_Ou2YF6Ce5xYeilxXBZ8f7ED4T1F4V2OwIPdBn46M8zBrxXTO4w?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password**

(Best overall)

Teams Starter Pack: around \$24.95/month for 10 users. Business: around \$8.99/user/month.

- Excellent user experience.
- Shared vaults for departments and projects.
- Granular access permissions.
- Strong admin and employee onboarding/offboarding tools.
- Excellent for non-technical teams.

Website: [1Password Business](https://1password.com/business)

---

![‎Bitwarden App - App Store](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/x38pyi5v1Vy6Zs97qz8ZgS0U3TY6bP46EZUol0vjWY-QJEsjpBL1sBYpo0AxExRZj59SXzc9D5J1hCMKpLCQRKtRmi0IYkc0CeiDQsrny4xPWuRz2OGsqZ9tyuMm4GtN5vMAwBBf6hXgHDHMP9_wXSBVttW9bXO5pQrWG4hhS-RxRNQIRTsbPrqb3y45Jv-M?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden**

(Best value)

Teams: around \$4/user/month, billed annually.

- Open-source foundations.
- Shared collections and organisational vaults.
- Good administrator controls.
- Supports self-hosting.
- Excellent security-to-price ratio.

Website: [Bitwarden Business](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![Keeper Security Logo PNG,  Vector (AI, EPS, CDR, PDF, SVG) - iconLogoVector](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hjZLLtGaZjkKvsDiCoIrNA749yx3vMYIFoRmmV0blB-pAj7O30nu3RJOVVhVRwgAOkJUfJ3datZ7pfH1wp7yeplrEL3FQ-HNOpCzlVOW0OcMr1CFjIFAx50apRkdH6sYOH31WcP6gfXOxeAN8qubYhHhGYA5yXp1bc7wqtCxjN2WEQuyMALTG1Pwne14BXyG?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper Security**

Business Starter around \$2/user/month; check plan limits.

- Strong administrative controls.
- Shared folders.
- Role-based permissions.
- Good compliance and security features.

Website: [Keeper Business](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

---

![‎Proton Pass - Password Manager App - App Store](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/TaoOIWJeIA3pvdLgQbFR3rAyw7BZDg22gSDBqQzjgf7aFWgDNikdL35h_JbfG6xl8YppIn7PtikWBfnKuSyKuWEoVqQbyjB7ehOz4glzG83bJqqO5l7wf88W3OcBNo5VIzlQqwPbpgx8qnioqfbijJYt-Rq1m2_kive4aba5KqPCTQAKSGo_4vSUTvN_qQz-?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Proton Pass**

Business plans from around \$2/user/month.

- Privacy-focused approach.
- Secure sharing.
- Email aliases.
- Attractive option for teams prioritising privacy.

Website: [Proton Pass for Business](https://proton.me/business/pass)

---

![Test Dashlane : un gestionnaire de mots de passe élégant et complet, mais trop avare - Les Numériques](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/66TJUMmYmc2uHzIsxHHiAx7hxRQ8alP8a248IQqZpKMw5qyY_k9MeFr4rutufsLjTYxUl32XmJycQKSNVtCaRTxRhBdFKuuN8SD7uZ8vs9JkSCZSzdZ2yIQm88TGjWCrg-h07fJdRP7X6VdOalsZe2e6fj_Ou1dMYyLIEbt_d4hajtzL8hVlKJz2qWk0Hm2z?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Dashlane**

Business pricing varies by plan.

- Polished interface.
- Password health monitoring.
- Security alerts and phishing protection.
- Useful security reporting.

Website: [Dashlane Business](https://www.dashlane.com/business)

Prices are indicative USD figures from November 2026, generally before tax. Confirm current UK pricing and VAT before purchasing. ## Quick comparison

| Feature | 1Password | Bitwarden |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Ease of use | Excellent | Very good |
| Shared passwords | Yes | Yes |
| Admin controls | Excellent | Very good |
| Open source | No | Yes |
| Self-hosting | No | Yes |
| Value for money | Good | Excellent |


## What I'd look for in a small business

Whichever you choose, make sure it supports\:

1. **Shared vaults** – staff can access company logins without sharing passwords over email or Slack.
2. **Individual accounts** – everyone has their own login.
3. **Granular permissions** – staff only see credentials they need.
4. **Easy offboarding** – revoke access immediately when someone leaves.
5. **Two-factor authentication** – protect the password manager itself.
6. **Audit logs** – know who accessed or changed shared credentials.

## A couple of questions to narrow it down

I can give you a much more specific recommendation with two details\:

**1\. How many people are in your team?**

2–5

5–10

10–25

25–50

More than 50

---

**2\. What's most important?**

Best balance of security and ease of use

Lowest possible cost

Maximum security and administrative control

Easy sharing of company passwords

---

**3\. What does your business primarily use?**

Microsoft 365

Google Workspace

A mixture of both

Neither / other
